title: Akai Ito

routes.title: 千羽烏月ルート
routes.notes: Senba Uzuki (千羽烏月, VNDB c10500). Reachable from the start; True End is『爽やかな立ち風』（ED32）, with ED3/13/28/29/30/31 as alternate endings. The original PS2 release and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system absent concrete behavioral-change evidence. The guide's main opening uses the Livedoor/Foxtail-supported『わたしはこくりと頷いた』path; XNEO's early-choice variants are treated as alternate valid routing, not a release difference. ED13『赤い縛め』requires an earlier no-chase state. Because no usable source-documented checkpoint exists before that required branch, ED13 is represented as a complete replay-from-beginning failed-play prefix using『追いかけない → 納得できない → 別に』, then the main Uzuki run begins fresh. Foxtail explicitly says the later night choice is absent when Uzuki was not met, so Livedoor's Save②『別に → 歯磨きはオッケー？』recovery combines incompatible branch states and is treated as a walkthrough error. XNEO/Lastcharles list an extra phone choice after the no-chase branch; because Foxtail marks『別に』itself as No.13 and says the later prompt is suppressed in that state, the guide treats that trailing phone entry as over-specified recovery shorthand rather than a required action. All six documented Uzuki save checkpoints remain on the main run.

routes.title: 若杉葛ルート
routes.notes: Wakasugi Tsuzura (若杉葛, VNDB c10498). The route's True End『彼岸の花をつかまえて』（ED12）requires first seeing ED11. PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system; Livedoor supplies detailed save/recovery checkpoints while XNEO and Foxtail independently resolve branch logic. All seven documented Tsuzura saves are preserved. The ED11 mirror decision is one choice: Livedoor's sequential『割るべきだと思う → 割るのは忍びない』listing is a walkthrough transcription/error, while XNEO and Foxtail show them as alternatives. The guide uses『割るのは忍びない』because it reaches ED11 and also satisfies the Tsuzura-side Nozomi route-seal condition. ED11 is resolved as『此岸と彼岸』from XNEO + Foxtail; Livedoor's『牝岸と彼岸』is treated as a title typo/variant, not a version difference.

routes.title: 浅間サクヤルート
routes.notes: Asama Sakuya (浅間サクヤ, VNDB c10499). Recommended after the required Uzuki/Tsuzura unlock work. True End is『ついのときまで』（ED25）; other documented endings are ED4/22-24/26-27. PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. All five source-documented Sakuya checkpoints are preserved: global Save14=local①, Save15=local②, Save16=local③, Save17=local④, Save18=local⑤; the ED23/26/24/27 recovery graph remains the already-flattened reachable structure. ED4『雫』has multiple valid documented paths; the guide emits the complete Livedoor replay-from-beginning path, while Foxtail red6 and the supplementary walkthrough are recorded as alternative routes to the same ending rather than version-specific behavior. ED22 also has multiple valid routes: Livedoor and the supplementary walkthrough support direct『見ているしかなかった → ED22』, while XNEO/Foxtail/the supplementary walkthrough support『飛び出していた → 月は蝕まれる運命なんだ → ED22』. The guide emits only the direct『見ているしかなかった』route and does not concatenate the two alternatives; Foxtail's『見ているしかなかった(No.22へ)』supports that branch choice. ED24 uses『凍てる孤月』based on Livedoor + Foxtail; XNEO's『凍てる弧月』is an orthographic source variant. ED26 is retained as Normal End because XNEO + Foxtail agree; Livedoor's Bad-End label is treated as a classification error/outlier.

routes.title: ユメイルート
routes.notes: Yumei (ユメイ, VNDB c10497). True End is『白花の咲く頃に』（ED21）; alternate endings are ED1/5/16-20. PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. The emitted opening『わたしはこくりと頷いた → 気のせいだと思い込む』is supported by Livedoor + Foxtail; differing XNEO opening choices are treated as alternate valid routing rather than a release change. All seven documented Yumei saves remain preserved. Yumei precedes Nozomi because the actual Nozomi seal requires completing an ending after『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』; XNEO's ED18 prerequisite wording is treated as shorthand for a route state that satisfies that underlying flag, not a different mechanic. ED20『赤い絆』is retained as Bad End from XNEO + Foxtail; Livedoor's Normal-End label is treated as a classification error/outlier.

routes.title: ノゾミルート
routes.notes: Nozomi (ノゾミ, VNDB c10502). PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. The underlying route seal is the pair documented by Livedoor + Foxtail red5: complete an ending after Tsuzura-route『割るのは忍びない』and complete an ending after Yumei-route『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』, opening『赤い縛め / 三日目 / 夜』. XNEO's Yumei-ED18 prerequisite is treated as shorthand/proxy for a prior route state that satisfies the Yumei-side seal, not a release-specific mechanic. The recommended order satisfies both flags before Nozomi. The route ends are Bad End『ニ重箱の底で』（ED14）and True End『光は風に』（ED15）;『ニ重箱』is retained from Livedoor + Foxtail, while differing orthography is treated as a source variant. No source designates ED15 as a single overarching true ending.

sources.title: アカイイト完全攻略 | XNEO
sources.notes: Set A component. Detailed Japanese text walkthrough covering all five routes, prerequisites, choices, ending names/numbers, and many alternate-ending paths. Although written for the original PS2 release, the owner-approved reconciliation treats PS2 and HD Remaster as the same route system absent concrete behavioral-change evidence; XNEO is therefore reconciled directly with Livedoor and Foxtail rather than treated as an obsolete-version source. Where it differs, the difference is classified as an alternate valid path, shorthand/omitted state, transcription/orthography issue, or walkthrough error.

sources.title: アカイイト/アカイイトHD REMASTER　攻略まとめ
sources.notes: Set A component. Directly inspected Japanese walkthrough explicitly covering both the original PS2 game and アカイイト HD REMASTER. It is especially useful for numbered save/checkpoint positions and compact ending-recovery sequences, but its HD label does not give it automatic priority over XNEO/Foxtail. Under the same-route-system premise, its disagreements are reconciled as branch-state shorthand or source errors where the state tables disagree. Known examples: the Uzuki ED13 Save② shortcut combines incompatible state (and incorrectly emits the later night choice), Tsuzura ED11 double-lists two alternatives, and its ED20/ED26 classifications are outliers.

sources.title: アカイイト攻略 分岐図 (Saomix Elements)
sources.notes: Historical/provenance source. The original FC2 site is dead and its archived branch-diagram images are not directly inspectable in the current reviewer environment, so it does not count toward the active Set B accuracy gate. Retained only because earlier research used it for cross-checking route/end-number history.

sources.title: FAQ/アカイイト攻略FAQ - アカイイト/アオイシロ まとめwiki
sources.notes: Partial/supplementary source, not a complete walkthrough on its own. Its FAQ section documents three specific hard-to-find choice sequences that are easy to miss on the branch diagram (烏月ルート「吸血鬼」の左, 烏月ルート「どうしてこんなところに？」の左→左, 葛ルート「コドク」の左, サクヤルート「歓迎の心は掃除から」の左→右), given as full choice chains. These were cross-checked against xneo.jp's day-by-day listings and are consistent. Also confirms there is no single canonical 'grand happy end' bugfix and that a specific ending ('言霊の継承(2)') has a known freeze bug unrelated to route logic. Site required a direct fetch with a browser user-agent (returns HTTP 403 to generic fetchers).

sources.title: アカイイト - ゲームカタログ@Wiki ～名作からクソゲーまで～
sources.notes: Reference/review article, not a choice-by-choice walkthrough. Used to corroborate structural facts: total of 32 endings (5 happy/True Ends, 12 Normal Ends, 15 Bad Ends); confirms only Uzuki's route needs no prior unlock ('ルートの解除をせずにいきなりハッピーエンドに到達出来るのは烏月だけ'); explicitly states there is NO single 'true happy end' among the 5 heroine True Ends ('「真のハッピーエンド」が存在しない...本当の意味でのハッピーエンドが存在しない'), and that the sequel Aoishiro added a 'Grand Happy End' specifically in response to this criticism (implying Akai Ito itself, including the 2023 HD Remaster, was not given one). Also supports the owner-approved reconciliation premise: the 2023 Switch/Steam 'AKAIITO HD REMASTER' is a remaster of the same content/routes as the original 2004 PS2 release, with no new routes added; no concrete route-behavior change is documented. Retrieved via Wayback Machine snapshot (direct fetch returns HTTP 403) at http://web.archive.org/web/20250303014011/https://w.atwiki.jp/gcmatome/pages/4086.html.

sources.title: PS２版「アカイイト」で全てのエンディングを見ました。- ルーファスの日記
sources.notes: Supplementary/opinion source only, not a walkthrough (no choice text). A completionist's blog post about having seen all 32 endings. Notable for a claim that conflicts with the guide's neutral 'no true end' framing: the author personally argues Yumei's True End is 'probably' the game's real true ending because the official drama CD's epilogue continues from a state consistent with her route. This is a personal interpretation, not corroborated by any walkthrough site, and is documented under disagreements rather than used to set is_true_ending on any route.

sources.title: Akai Ito - VNDB entry v98
sources.notes: Reference only. Confirms release history: original PS2 release (2004-08/10), SuperLite 2000 budget re-release (2005), PSN download (2013), and the newest release, 'AKAIITO HD REMASTER' for Nintendo Switch and Steam/PC (2023-05-25), bundled with a HD Remaster of the sequel Aoishiro. The 2023 HD Remaster is the release targeted for this guide per project rules (most recent platform). Release-history reference only. No concrete evidence was found that the HD Remaster changed route/ending behavior; walkthrough disagreements are therefore not treated as version differences without separate behavioral evidence.

sources.title: VNDB Kana API — character list for v98
sources.notes: Reference only, used to obtain exact, non-hallucinated VNDB character IDs and portrait image URLs (queried directly via the API rather than relying on a scraped/summarized page, to avoid transcription errors in image IDs). Confirmed 5 characters with vns.role = 'primary' for v98: Yumei (c10497), Wakasugi Tsuzura (c10498), Asama Sakuya (c10499), Senba Uzuki (c10500), Nozomi (c10502) — these are the 5 heroine routes. Protagonist is Hatou Kei (c10490, role 'main'). Side characters Kei/ケイ (c10507, twin brother, distinct from protagonist despite same reading), Nushi (c10509), Mikage (c10856), and Nara Youko (c91338, no portrait image available) are not route characters.

sources.title: AKAIITO HD REMASTER 攻略
sources.notes: Supplementary Japanese walkthrough, not counted as Set A or Set B. Used only to reconcile branch-state disputes: it corroborates the earlier no-chase requirement for Uzuki ED13, documents multiple valid Sakuya ED4 routes, and explicitly describes two alternative Sakuya ED22 paths (direct『見ているしかなかった』or『飛び出していた → 月は蝕まれる運命なんだ』). Its HD label is not treated as evidence that the underlying route system changed.

disagreements: Owner-approved reconciliation premise: treat the original PS2 release and アカイイト HD REMASTER as the same route/ending system unless a source provides concrete evidence that game behavior changed. The inspected sources provide no such evidence. Walkthrough disagreements are therefore resolved as alternative valid paths, omitted prerequisite state / abbreviated recovery instructions, transcription or orthography differences, or walkthrough errors—not speculative PS2-vs-HD mechanics. 1) There is no single overarching 'true ending'; each heroine has her own True End. 2) Opening-choice differences between XNEO and Livedoor/Foxtail are treated as alternate valid routing or transcription variants when they do not change the represented ending logic; the guide uses an internally reachable path supported by the active source set. 3) Nozomi unlock wording: XNEO's Yumei-ED18 prerequisite is shorthand/proxy; Livedoor + Foxtail expose the underlying Tsuzura『割るのは忍びない』+ ending and Yumei『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』+ ending route-seal flags. 4) Uzuki ED13: the required earlier no-chase state is corroborated by XNEO, Foxtail, and the supplementary walkthrough. Foxtail explicitly says the later night choice is absent in that state, so Livedoor's Save②『別に → 歯磨きはオッケー？』recovery is a state-combining walkthrough error. XNEO/Lastcharles list a trailing phone choice after the no-chase route, but Foxtail marks『別に』itself No.13 and says the later prompt is suppressed; the guide therefore ends the ED13 replay after『別に』and treats the extra phone entry as over-specified recovery shorthand, not a release difference. 5) Sakuya ED4: Livedoor, XNEO/Foxtail red6, and the supplementary walkthrough document different valid paths to the same ED4. The guide emits one complete replay-from-beginning path and records the others as alternatives. 6) Sakuya ED22: there are at least two valid routes—direct『見ているしかなかった → ED22』(Livedoor + supplementary walkthrough; Foxtail marks the choice No.22) and『飛び出していた → 月は蝕まれる運命なんだ → ED22』(XNEO + Foxtail + supplementary walkthrough). The guide emits only the direct route; concatenating the two is incorrect. 7) ED26『月へ向かう蝶』: XNEO + Foxtail classify it Normal End; Livedoor says Bad End. This is treated as a Livedoor classification error/outlier, and the guide retains Normal End. 8) ED24『凍てる孤月』: Livedoor + Foxtail support『孤月』while XNEO prints『弧月』; this is treated as an orthographic source variant, not a version difference. 9) Tsuzura ED11: Livedoor accidentally double-lists the mutually exclusive mirror choices and prints『牝岸と彼岸』; XNEO + Foxtail show the choices as alternatives and support『此岸と彼岸』. The guide uses『割るのは忍びない』and『此岸と彼岸』. 10) Yumei ED20『赤い絆』: XNEO + Foxtail classify it Bad End; Livedoor says Normal End. This is treated as a Livedoor classification error/outlier, and the guide retains Bad End. 11) Historical Saomix material remains provenance-only and is not part of the active verification gate.
